chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah narrated from al-'Abbas, from Hammad ibn 'Isa and 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Ibn Sinan, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi 'Abd Allah, who said:
I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about the muhrim who dies: how is he to be treated?

He said: "'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan عليه السلام died at al-Abwa' with al-Husayn عليه السلام while he was in ihram. And with al-Husayn were 'Abd Allah ibn al-'Abbas and 'Abd Allah ibn Ja'far. He was treated as the deceased is treated, his face was covered, and no perfume was applied to him."
He said: "And that was in the Book of 'Ali عليه السلام."

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah
key_terms.بِالْأَبْوَاءِ: at al-Abwa', the location where the event occurred
key_terms.بِالْمَيِّتِ: the deceased person and the normal funerary treatment applied to him
key_terms.طِيبًا: perfume or scent, which was not to be applied
key_terms.كِتَابِ عَلِيٍّ: the Book of 'Ali عليه السلام, cited as the source of the ruling
key_terms.وَجْهُهُ: his face, mentioned here regarding covering it

ai.seo_question: How should a muhrim be treated after death in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for a person who dies while in ihram during hajj or 'umrah. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام cites the case of 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hasan عليه السلام to show that such a deceased person is treated like other dead persons, except that perfume is not applied, and he attributes this ruling to the Book of 'Ali عليه السلام.
